interface.title: AmpliQA
interface.field: Molecular biology: RT-qPCR measurement of gene expression
interface.stage_of_work: Planning the experiment, bench work (RNA quantification, cDNA synthesis, plate setup), then data analysis, statistics and writing up
interface.what_it_is_for: Takes an RT-qPCR gene-expression experiment from plan to paper: a step schedule, NanoDrop quality checks and cDNA pipetting volumes, qPCR plate maps, Ct import and QC, reference-gene-normalised fold change, a recommended statistical test, publication figures, and draft Methods/Results text. All of it is kept in a downloadable .xlsx experiment file.

data.note: Most of the work used the built-in fictitious zebrafish example ('Load the example experiment': 3 groups × 3 pools, reference gene actb1, targets bdnf/sox2/cdnf), plus 'Use an example run' on the qPCR import tab. Before that I started a blank experiment (mouse brain, 3 groups × 4 samples, 2 per pool) and typed one NanoDrop reading by hand. Example NanoDrop .tsv and Rotor-Gene .csv files downloaded fine, but I could not upload them back: the upload tool only accepts files from the test-data folder, which is empty. From the Groups step on, the target gene cdnf was also made a second reference gene to try multi-reference normalisation, so every downstream number (stability, fold change, statistics, methods text) uses actb1 + cdnf, a normaliser set no one would really choose.

features.name: Multi-reference normalisation with stability check

Export log2 fold change as GraphPad Prism tables
serves_tasks: Set the normalisers and correction factors
Check controls, replicate agreement and normaliser stability

features.name: Assumption-driven test recommender with manual override
features.general: Choose a group-comparison test automatically from normality and equal-variance checks and the question asked (vs control or all pairs), explain the choice, screen for outliers, and let the user force a different test
features.specific: Statistics: Test scale (ΔCt), Question (each group vs control → Dunnett; all pairs → Tukey), 'Choose the test manually' (ANOVA, Welch, Kruskal-Wallis, t-tests, Mann-Whitney; post hoc), per-gene details with Shapiro-Wilk, Brown-Forsythe, post-hoc table, Grubbs outliers. Bug: a manual Kruskal-Wallis with post hoc on 'Automatic' keeps the automatic Tukey, and the methods text then says 'Kruskal-Wallis followed by Tukey'
steps: Read the summary table of tests and p-values
Expand a gene to see why the test was chosen and the outlier check
Optionally override the test, and set the post hoc by hand too (e.g. Dunn for Kruskal-Wallis), since 'Automatic' keeps the recommended one
serves_tasks: Run the appropriate group comparison with assumption checks and outlier screening
